Prompt delivery upon order is critical to support ongoing medical and personal care services, helping Veterans maintain their independence and health in their home environment. Delays could disrupt essential care routines, impacting the well-being of Veterans who rely on these supplies for daily living and therapeutic needs. The estimated value of this action is $9,420,031.56 with a period of performance of six (6) months with a three (3) month base period and one (1) three (3) month option period.

Office of Procurement, Acquisition and Logistics (OPAL) Strategic Acquisition Center (SAC) 10300 Spotsylvania Avenue, Suite 400 Fredericksburg, Virginia 22408 While other vendors can offer the required beds, the incumbent’s established delivery network uniquely positions it as the only responsible source, ensuring timely and reliable fulfillment of the agency’s requirements. This proven infrastructure supports uninterrupted supply continuity and minimizes risk of delay, factors critical to meeting the Veterans’ needs. The contract requires delivery of specialized in-home hospital beds and accessories to the individual VAMCs, with free on-board (FOB) destination, in accordance with the specific delivery instructions contained within the delivery orders. The contractor shall deliver to any VAMC within the United States and its outlying Territories and areas to include the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, Alaska, and Hawaii upon issuance of a delivery order. The contractor shall also provide a commercial warranty in accordance with industry standards. The contractor must guarantee their ability to provide an uninterrupted source of supply of the awarded devices to satisfy the Government’s requirements for the effective period of the contract. The current contractor has the required supply chain in place to fulfill orders on a nationwide basis. Onboarding a new vendor to fulfill this requirement and deliver the hospital beds and accessories before the expiration of the current contract is not possible and would introduce delays and increased costs that would prevent timely performance and compromise patient care and safety. A new vendor would require at least 45 days to become fully operational. Therefore, Invacare is the only responsible source uniquely positioned to fulfill orders received from VAMCs in a timely manner. Invacare has provided an uninterrupted source of supply and commercial warranty of the hospital beds and accessories since 2020 and has delivered to locations within the United States and US Territories. From July 2023 through March 2025, under the previously awarded 5-year contract 36C10G18D0018, Invacare provided over in-home hospital beds or accessories to Veterans across the nation, demonstrating the capability to fulfill both standard and large-scale orders. Invacare is immediately capable of meeting all requirements of the contract and has the required capabilities to deliver the necessary products without interruption in supply or degradation of quality of care to the Veteran. Cost Savings: Without a bridge contract, VA would lack a National Contract vehicle to provide in-home hospital beds and accessories to Veterans in the community and VAMCs will be required to purchase the items through local Network Contracting Offices (NCO’s), potentially at open market prices, which would result in major financial loss to the Government and significantly delay the time it takes for the Veteran to receive the clinically required items.

This determination will be based on a comparison of current contract pricing, past proposal submissions (if available), other information made available, and an Independent Government Cost Estimate. (8) A description of the market research conducted (see part 10) and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted. Additional market research was completed and it was determined no vendors can be operational in the timeframe needed, as a new vendor would require at least 45 days to become fully operational. A significant amount of market research was completed for the follow-on procurement which supports competition as a long-term strategy. However, a bridge contract is necessary in the interim to avoid a lapse in the immediate availability of these unique supplies to Veterans. The System for Award Management (SAM) Responsibility / Qualification (formerly Federal Awardee Performance, and Integrity Information System (FAPIIS)) was reviewed and SAM shows no reports for Invacare Corp that would indicate defective pricing, instances of contractor fault or recipient not- qualified, terminations for cause, default, material failure to comply, or non-responsibility of the contractor. The NAICS code for this effort is 339113 Surgical Appliance and Supplies Manufacturing industry. These are commercial products. (9) Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition. The Strategic Acquisition Center is actively working on a follow-on contract. In the interim, a bridge contract will prevent a disruption in the delivery of critical medical equipment to our nation’s Veterans. Ensuring that Veterans’ needs will continue to be supported while the follow-on contract is procured is essential to accomplishing the VA mission of delivering world class health care to our nation’s Veterans.
